# Local signed 0.3.0 implementation plan

Goal: build a local-only 0.3.0 package signed through SimplySign, support Steam
Play using the saved launcher settings, and document voluntary support.
Initial scope was local only. The user subsequently authorized publishing 0.3.0
to GitHub with a humorous EAC/use-at-your-own-risk changelog note.

Design: keep the existing process-local OpenXR layer setup and executable guard.
Steam launch options invoke the launcher with `--steam %command%`. Validate the
forwarded executable against the configured LMU executable, preserve arguments,
ensure +XR, auto-launch and keep the benchmark UI alive until the game exits.
Expose a copyable Steam launch option in Setup; no global layer registration or
game DLL replacement. This is an implementation choice within the requested
Steam-start behavior. A global implicit layer would affect unrelated sessions;
a game-folder proxy adds another injected DLL and installation lifecycle.

- [x] Regression tests for Steam argument parsing, wrong/missing executable,
  Windows quoting round trips, existing +XR, and retained provider environment.
- [x] Implement Steam launch helper, launcher entry point and Setup copy action;
  update build/tests and verify full launcher suite and layout.
- [x] Set VERSION 0.3.0, update docs/changelog with certificate purchase and
  confirmed coffee/affiliate/Patreon links; support never required or expected,
  tool always free. Retain removed dynamic FOV status and prior fixes.
- [x] Build native code, sign distributed DLL/EXEs with SHA256 and RFC3161,
  verify publisher/timestamp and package only after signing. Verify ZIP hashes.
- [ ] Configure the local Steam launch option and verify the game loads the
  signed layer; record any runtime/headset limits. Keep everything local.

Review focus: no shell execution of forwarded arguments, unsupported game guard
retained, missing/malformed settings fail before launch, correct Steam lifecycle,
all packaged executables signed, hash manifest generated after signing.

Validation: the new regression first failed because Steam support was missing;
native and launcher full build/test scripts subsequently passed. A fresh review
found no important code defects and independently verified three signatures.
All 38 packaged file hashes and all three timestamped signatures were verified.
The user stopped computer control with Escape before the Steam launch option
could be applied. Steam was left unchanged; live Steam/LMU lifecycle and headset
validation remain pending. No push, remote tag or release action was performed.

Publication follow-up: retain the reviewed and signed binaries; update release
documentation, regenerate the ZIP and verify signed bytes and manifest hashes
before committing/pushing main and publishing v0.3.0. Disclose the pending live
Steam test in the release notes. Do not imply code signing grants EAC approval.
